nodes.label: failover.recovery.outcome.total (per-method outcome counter)
nodes.rationale: One counter recorded once per intercepted method call (a findAll() is one event, not one per entity) yields all three operational rates. It is tagged by method so two methods sharing a name/domain stay distinguishable, and 'error' is kept distinct from 'not_recovered' so a store/serialization fault is never miscounted as a clean miss.

nodes.label: FailoverMeterBinder gauges
nodes.rationale: failover.live.entries is registered only when the store can report size — always for in-memory/Caffeine, JDBC only when opted in, because it costs a SELECT COUNT(*) per scrape (audit A7). Not available in multi-tenant mode.

nodes.label: failover.store.async.failed counter
nodes.rationale: Async write failures are swallowed so they never break the business call, which would silently degrade the store layer — this counter keeps that visible. It covers both in-flight failure and submit-time rejection, closing the gap where a saturated executor dropped writes unmetered. DISCARD deliberately does not increment it because discarding is configured behaviour, not a failure; use ABORT if every dropped write must be alertable.

nodes.label: Kibana dashboard via micrometer-registry-elastic
nodes.rationale: The elastic registry pushes existing failover.* meters, so Kibana visualizations need no additional instrumentation.

nodes.label: Structured log levels (INFO name-only, DEBUG full payload)
nodes.rationale: Lifecycle events stay at INFO carrying only the referential name and the full payload body moved to DEBUG so high-throughput services pay no full-payload serialisation on the INFO path (ADR 48).
